citation: Vroblesky, D.A., and Petkewich, M.D., 2009, Investigation of contaminated groundwater at Solid Waste Management Unit 12, Naval Weapons Station Charleston, North Charleston, South Carolina, 2008: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report SIR-2009-5166, map scale 1:1,176.
notes:
Pages 1-35: report text (site history, methods, hydrology, contamination, summary), references, appendix 1 (well construction, pp. 26-27) and the first part of appendix 2 (monthly water levels, pp. 28-35; continues in the next packet). Each appendix 1 well is one observation (State Plane coordinates, ground elevation, installation date, screened interval in ft bgs; for 12PZ- wells without ground elevation the screen depths are below top of casing). Only the last water level in appendix 2 (8/28/2008) is recorded per well; earlier monthly levels and contaminant concentrations (figures 5-10) are not recorded. Table columns are paired by position and flagged inferred. General sampling-method references (Barcelona, Sevee, Shanklin, Vogel, Vroblesky 2007b) skipped.
Pages 36-53: end of appendix 2 (monthly water levels for wells 12MW-26S to 12PZ-04; only the 8/28/2008 level recorded, wells not measured that day skipped) and appendix 3 (organic-compound concentrations in groundwater and surface water, pp. 38-53, continuing in the next packet). Water-chemistry concentrations have no field in the extraction schema and were not recorded.
Pages 54-72: end of appendix 3 (organic-compound concentrations in groundwater and marsh surface water) and start of appendix 4 (inorganic constituents and field properties in groundwater). Water-chemistry concentrations have no field in the extraction schema; nothing recorded.
Pages 73-86: rest of appendix 4 (inorganic constituents and field properties in groundwater) and back matter. Water-chemistry values have no field in the extraction schema; nothing recorded.
